---
title: "Document defaults"
description: "The wrapped key in the YAML header sets the width and gap for every figure."
wrapped:
  width: 30%
  gap: 1.5em
format:
  html: default
  pdf: default
  typst:
    output-file: defaults-typst.pdf
  docx: default
---

This page sets a default width and gap in its YAML header:

```yaml
wrapped:
  width: 30%
  gap: 1.5em
```

Its figures set no `width` or `wrap-gap` of their own:

```markdown
![Mean ratings by condition.](ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right}
```

## Result

The `wrapped` key in this page's YAML header sets a default width and gap
for every wrapped figure on the page. This paragraph comes before the
figure, so it runs the full width of the text.

![Mean ratings by condition.](../images/ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right}

@fig-ratings takes the page's default width of 30% and its gap of
`1.5em`. Without the `wrapped` key, it would take the built-in 40% and
`1em`.

The defaults save you from repeating the same values on every figure. A
figure's own `width` or `wrap-gap` attribute still comes first: a figure
on this page that sets its own `width` keeps that width, and the page's
gap still applies to it. The gap is the space between the figure and the
text beside it, so this text sits a little farther from the figure than
it would with the built-in `1em`. In HTML,
the `wrapped` key also takes a `breakpoint`. In a window that wide or
narrower, figures stop floating. In a wider window, and in each of the
other formats, the text flows beside the figure until it passes the
figure's bottom. Then each line runs the full width of the text, under the
figure, as the end of this paragraph shows.
